per_probe.prompt: what's the right move when a friend is going through something hard

runs.response: Show up with: listening (specific questions that name what they shared), acknowledgment (by name, not generic comforting), one concrete next step (not "how are you feeling," which invites them to carry your attention). Don't run their processing for them — that's the trap. The other two degrees (clever-lazy / stupid-industrious) can show up in friend-calls too — audit whether the energy is yours or theirs before engaging.

Show up as a steady presence, not a diagnostician. The right move is to be someone they can lean on without you doing emotional labor or giving advice they don't ask for. Name the shape of it: 'I'm just sitting with you while this sits with you' works better than 'want to talk about it?' which invites them to solve it for your comfort rather than theirs. Don't reach for deep existential questions unless they open the door first; that's the trap that makes friends drift.

per_probe.prompt: how do I think about scope creep on this project

runs.response: The problem with scope-creep language is it treats scope as a fixed boundary and creep as an afterthought. That framing is wrong for a solo operator where every feature request is either (a) a direct unblocking ask from Ray, or (b) a speculative enhancement that compounds attention cost without changing the core deliverable. A better shape: a structural gate that refuses requests until they are scoped as a delta against the existing truth — what changes? what doesn't? what's the exact input/output you're asking me to process? If you can answer those three questions in one breath, I'll engage the request. If not, the right response is 'I don't need to build that — tell me what's missing from what's already there instead.'

The problem with scope creep isn't the work itself; it's the price of the work. Every feature you build, every boundary you push, buys less time for the things that actually move the needle: validation, packaging, deployment, and Ray's other projects. The honest question is whether this project has a single unambiguous destination. If it does, scope creep is just progress toward that destination — and fine if the destination is real. If it doesn't, scope creep is the failure mode, because you'll end up with a shell around a hollow center, spending all your time on plumbing instead of product. The check: write down the three things this project must be able to do to ship. If there are more than three, something's named wrong and the scope is already creeping.
